title: User-Centred Design
body:
**User-centred design** makes the person's goals the starting point of every decision, rather
than the structure of the implementation.

Its practical content is one warning: the designer is not the user. A developer knows the
system's model, has seen every state it can be in, and cannot recover the experience of not
knowing. Anything that feels obvious to them is evidence about them alone.

```
implementation-driven    the interface exposes whatever shape the database has,
                         and the user learns the schema
user-centred             the interface follows what the user is trying to do,
                         and the schema stays hidden
```

The method that follows is a cycle: find out who the user is with a [[User Persona]] and a
[[Task Analysis]], build a cheap [[Prototyping|prototype]], test it with
[[Usability Testing]], and repeat. Each pass is meant to discard work, which is why the
early passes have to be cheap.

The claim underneath is that usability is measurable. Task completion rate, time on task and
error count are numbers, so two designs can be compared with evidence, and a disagreement about
them stops being a matter of preference, and [[Human Capabilities]] supplies the
constraints that predict which will win.
